rawQuotes.quote: Can you connect the polar beat app to the training section. I am a rower and cannot record/video my sessions so it’s easier to log my heart rate with the training.
rawQuotes.note: In-app feature · Malcolm's bot filed TRY-576 (Need Approval)

rawQuotes.quote:
Hey guys! First of all, I just want to say that I love this app sooo much!! It keeps me motivated without being distracting, which I really appreciate! 

One feature I think would be super nice to add is the option to assign two categories to the same study session at once!

For example, let’s say I study math for 30 minutes. I’d love to be able to track those 30 minutes under both “Studying” and “Math” at the same time. Right now I can only split the time between categories, so e.g. I’d have to track 20 minutes as “Studying” and the remaining 10 minutes as “Math”

But what I’d actually want is for both categories to count the full 30 minutes, since I was studying and in specific I was studying math, if that makes sense.

So when I look back at my statistics, I can see how much time I’ve spent studying overall, but also how much time I’ve dedicated to each specific subject, without having to split up my sessions.

I absolutely love this app already I know it’s going to go huge.

rawQuotes.quote:
Hi Eddie,

Juan here. I found Latent on Instagram and I have been digging into it
as a founder, not a user.

I built something a while back called equity. Same idea as yours at
the core, an accountability app where you bet money on yourself. $20
says you hit the gym at 6am every day. It died on one problem:
verification. A workout is easy to certify. Reading a book or doing
deep work on a computer is not. How do you prove you did the thing?

Your timelapse approach is clever. Presence on camera, clock stops
when you switch apps. But I keep coming back to the same wall. What
stops someone from sitting at a desk for two hours doing nothing? And
how do you handle work that does not happen on the phone at all?

Genuinely curious how far you have taken the verification layer, and
where you think it breaks.

Juan
